TENDRILS ACROSS THE OPENING: fine green tendrils reaching from one jamb to the other across a narrow gap, tips curling around empty air, the thinnest stems catching and holding themselves mid-span
ROOTS GRIPPING THE BLOCK: two fat root arms curled around a single dressed stone, knuckled and pale, each finger pressing into a joint as though the root measured the block before it held
ROOTS LIFTING THE FLAGSTONES: a spread of old roots running just under a flagstone floor, pressing each slab into a gentle wave, the joints cracked open and lined with dark soft earth
ROOT ARCH THROUGH THE GAP: a root grown sideways through a broken gap in a wall, bending down on the far side and back into the ground, forming a low arch a person could duck beneath
MOSS ON EVERY STAIR TREAD: soft moss furring every horizontal step in a velvet stripe of green, the risers pale stone, the treads thick enough that a foot would leave a print in the pile
LICHEN MAP ON THE PILLAR: pale silver-green lichen spread across a drum column in irregular patches, each patch edged cleanly, the whole pillar mapped in soft continents of grey-green and gold-green
FERNS FROM THE CRACKS: fern fronds unrolling from the joints between courses, each one a fresh pale spiral opening into a full dark-green blade, the wall softened into a vertical garden
VELVET CAP ON THE DRUM: a fallen column drum lying on its side with a dense cap of velvet moss grown over the top face, deep green and perfectly level, the curved sides still bare pale stone

SLIM TREE THROUGH THE STAIRWELL: a slim straight tree growing up through the open well of a stone stair, its trunk rising past each landing, bark smooth and grey-green, the canopy level with the top course

BROAD CANOPY OVER THE CHAMBER: a large tree standing inside a roofless chamber, its wide canopy resting on the air above the four walls, the branches reaching every corner, leaves filling the open square of sky
SAPLINGS ALONG THE WALL TOP: a row of young trees growing from the rubble along a wall's coping, roots down into the joints, trunks upright and evenly spaced, the whole line reading as a living hedge

CLEAR WATER ACROSS THE FLOOR: still green water standing across a stone floor to ankle depth, the submerged slabs visible through the clarity, the surface perfectly flat and faintly reflecting the green above

SEAGRASS ON THE SUBMERGED BLOCKS: ribbons of seagrass leaning together over submerged stone blocks, small bright corals crusting the lower courses in orange and white, the water clear enough to count the joints

SPRING THROUGH THE FLAGSTONES: a spring welling up through a lifted corner of flagstone, the water spreading in a thin bright sheet across the floor, the stone around the gap dark and smooth from the constant flow

WATER FROM THE BROKEN CHANNEL: a thin fall of water dropping from the open end of a broken stone channel, landing in a small pool on the floor below, the stone around the pool bearded in wet green moss
DUNES TO THE PILLAR'S WAIST: pale sand banked in smooth curves against a row of pillars, each dune rising to the waist of the column, the windward face steep and the lee face a long gentle slope

SAND FAN THROUGH THE DOORWAY: dry sand drifted through a doorway in a perfect fan shape, the widest edge spreading across the interior floor, the grains sorted fine at the tip and coarser at the edges
FLOOR HALF-BURIED IN SAND: a stone floor buried under blown sand to half its depth, only the top edges of the paving blocks still showing as a faint grid of lines across the pale drifted surface

WILDFLOWERS ON THE FALLEN TERRACE: a dense mat of small wildflowers covering a collapsed terrace, white and yellow and pale violet blooms held on thin stems above a base of fine green leaves, every crack full

BLOSSOM TREES OVER THE COURTYARD WALL: two blossom trees leaning over a courtyard wall from inside, their branches crossing the coping and hanging a curtain of pale pink flowers down the outer face of the stone
CORDS LACING THE ARCH: thick creeper cords wound through every stone of the arch in a slow green lace, each cord fat and smooth, pressing into the mortar joints and pulling gently along the curve

WALL STITCHED IN SMALL LEAVES: a whole face of stone covered in a flat mat of small round leaves, each one a bright green pixel pressed flush to the surface, the pattern dense and even from block to block

FLOWERING CREEPER AT THE WINDOW: a flowering creeper spilling from a high window opening in a loose cascade, pale blossoms sitting open among the leaves, trailing stems hanging a full storey down the outer face

TENDRILS ACROSS THE OPENING: fine green tendrils reaching from both jambs of a wide opening, tips just touching at the centre, the slender cords strung with small paired leaves in a soft repeating pattern
ROOTS GRIPPING THE BLOCK: a single large root wrapped around a corner block like a fist, each rounded finger pressed into the stone face, the grip confident and tight all the way to the ground

FLAGSTONES LIFTED INTO WAVES: roots running beneath a wide floor and pressing up, lifting the flagstones into long gentle waves, each slab tilted slightly from the next in a slow undulation across the whole surface
ROOT ARCH THROUGH THE GAP: two roots grown from opposite sides of a gap in the wall, arching toward each other and fusing at the crown into a single smooth pale arch that fills the space cleanly
